title: Delegation of Authority Explained | Principles of Management Ep 25
description:
What happens when every small decision waits for the boss? In this animated lesson, Chai Corner now has five outlets and a small head office. At outlet 2, Meena has to call Ravi for every refund and every milk order, Ravi gets forty calls a day, and customers wait.

You will learn what delegation of authority means: a manager gives a team member the authority to do a task and make decisions about it. We cover the three linked elements of delegation (responsibility, authority and accountability), the key rule (authority can be delegated, responsibility is assigned and accepted, but accountability cannot be delegated, so the manager stays ultimately accountable), the principle of parity (authority must match responsibility), and the benefits of delegation: it frees the manager, develops the team and speeds up decisions.

This is Episode 25 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 Forty calls a day
0:24 What is delegation of authority?
0:40 Responsibility, authority, accountability
1:07 What moves down, what stays up
1:29 Principle of parity
1:47 Benefits of delegation
2:03 Quick check
2:17 Recap
